drugRefs.duration: 3-6 weeks (transition to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate once improving)
drugRefs.why: Reliable anaerobic and streptococcal coverage appropriate for the prolonged course required in lung abscess; IV therapy initially with oral step-down once clinically stable.

drugRefs.coverage: Strong anaerobic coverage; historically first-line, though beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitors are now generally preferred given clindamycin resistance trends.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Ampicillin-sulbactam covers the core polymicrobial anaerobic flora reliably.
gaps: MRSA not covered — add if specific risk factors or culture-confirmed.

stewardship.deescalation: Transition from IV to oral once afebrile and clinically improving (often 1-2 weeks), continuing oral therapy to complete the total 3-6 week course; reassess imaging if response is slow to exclude an underlying obstructing lesion (e.g., malignancy).

framework: Prolonged duration (weeks, not days) is appropriate for lung abscess given the necrotizing, slow-resolving nature of the infection — do not apply standard CAP duration logic here.
Image-guided or surgical drainage should be considered for large abscesses (>6-8cm) or those failing to respond to antibiotics alone.
Transition to oral therapy once clinically improving rather than continuing IV for the entire prolonged course.
